You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from Riverview Task 1 2017-18 · Essay (a Riverview Year 12 Business Studies assessment, Operations topic) strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 1 [20 marks]: Assess strategies that operations management may use to respond to influences of technology, quality expectations and corporate social responsibility.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 20):
17–20 marks: Makes a well-reasoned judgement regarding how operations management has responded to technology, quality expectations and corporate social responsibility. Applies relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues. Presents a sustained, logical and cohesive response and communicates clearly using relevant business terminology and concepts.
13–16 marks: Makes some judgement regarding how operations management has responded to technology, quality expectations and corporate social responsibility. Uses relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues. Presents a logical and cohesive response using relevant business terminology and concepts.
9–12 marks: Provides characteristics and features of operations management and technology, quality expectations and/or corporate social responsibility. May make reference to case study/studies and contemporary business issues. Communicates using business terminology and concepts.
5–8 marks: Sketches in general terms operations management and/or influences in the business environment. May make reference to case study/studies and/or contemporary business issues. Communicates using some business terminology and concepts.
1–4 marks: Makes limited reference to operations management and/or influences in the business environment. May identify case study/studies. Uses basic business terminology.


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Strategies responding to technology: leading edge and established technology, new product design, SCM (e-commerce), overcoming resistance to change. Quality expectations: quality management (control, assurance, improvement, TQM), performance objectives of quality and dependability. CSR: environmental sustainability in inputs and processes, ethical sourcing (global sourcing, outsourcing decisions), legal compliance versus ethical responsibility. Operations strategies: performance objectives (quality, speed, dependability, flexibility, customisation, cost); new product or service design and development; supply chain management (logistics, e-commerce, global sourcing); outsourcing (advantages and disadvantages); technology (leading edge, established); inventory management (advantages and disadvantages of holding stock, LIFO, FIFO, JIT); quality management (control, assurance, improvement); overcoming resistance to change (financial costs, purchasing new equipment, redundancy payments, retraining, reorganising plant layout, inertia); global factors (global sourcing, economies of scale, scanning and learning, research and development).

TEACHER MARKER COMMENTS:
Better responses explained the appropriate terms (quality control, quality assurance and continuous improvement) and then used their case study to support the response, relating case studies to specific changes in the operational process and providing statistics (metrics) to show how responses to the influences affected operations management, rather than just profit and revenue. Lesser responses provided statistics not related to operations strategies (especially for CSR, where marketing issues were often present), or became a general discussion of the case study without specific reference to the question. Some responses showed a lack of planning: unfinished last part, no logical progression, minimal paragraphs. One idea per paragraph. Answer the question asked.


STUDENT RESPONSE:

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-20>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '17–20'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a 6 to 8 line plan of what a full-mark response would cover, one line per paragraph, not a full essay>"}
